newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent crude extends gains, wet looks to follow.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent crude extends gains, wet looks to follow.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude extended early paper gains on Monday afternoon, lifted by investment fund buying on futures markets, and wet differentials started to follow, traders said.

Talk of a tighter spot market in June due to scheduled maintenance in the North Sea and stronger IPE futures, helped by tension in the Middle East, pushed the prompt June/July intermonth spread out to +13 cents from +8 cents late on Friday.
"The spread has gone out a bit which is helping (spot) differentials but there's been no big change in this market on the physical side," said a trader.
No Dated Brent deals were reported by midafternoon on Monday but traders said a May 25-27 cargo was offered at June Brent -5 cents, 23 cents firmer than the last June-related deal almost a week ago.
June IPE Brent futures jumped sharply, gaining 61 cents to $19.54 a barrel by 1541 GMT as a strong U.S. opening added to early strength prompted by new Iranian wargames in the Gulf.
The July/August cash spread also strengthened, trading at +7 cents after early talk around +3 cents.
"The spreads are rising with vengeance...They tend to go in jerks, the market is on a roll upwards," one trader said.
"There's a lot of focus now on the maintenance programmes in June and people are suddenly feeling that the market could be tight for June for North Sea (crudes)...," he added.
Brent CFDs were also firmer, this week's dates gaining 13 cents to talk at July Brent +4/+5 cents. May 19-23 was bid at July Brent -4 cents.
One Brent cargo was turning wet on Monday with a loading date of May 27-29, traders said.
On wet markets, a May 23-25 Gullfaks C cargo traded at Dated Brent +16 cents, 11 cents firmer than a deal last Wednesday for a cargo loading May 15-17.
Traders also reported talk of an Oseberg trade but the price could not be confirmed.
